data.narrative:
Chaos Industries is a Series D defense and security company currently valued at $4.5B post-money following $1B+ in cumulative fundraising. The valuation assessment draws from a comparable universe of 10 companies: 2 public peers (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms, with particular focus on 4 same-stage, same-sector private comparables including Saronic ($9.2B), Quantum-Systems ($8.0B), True Anomaly ($2.2B), and Onebrief ($2.1B).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.5x step-up multiplier typical of Series D advancement to the last post-money valuation, yielding $6.8B. Peer-median analysis across the 4 same-sector Series D comparables produces a median valuation of $5.1B, with a range spanning $2.1B to $9.2B. These comparable companies exhibit substantial dispersion, reflecting heterogeneity in scale, technology maturity, or market positioning within the defense tech sector.

The two-method triangulation supports a valuation range of $4.3B (low) to $7.8B (high), with a median of $5.9B. The current $4.5B post-money sits at the lower end of this range. Key uncertainties include whether Chaos Industries' technology differentiation and customer traction align with higher-quartile peers like Saronic and Quantum-Systems, or lower-quartile comparables. The wide peer dispersion ($2.1B–$9.2B) underscores material sensitivity to company-specific fundamentals not captured in stage and sector alone.
